parity-metronoid-first-moment-repacking.statement:
Let \(r,d\ge1\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^r\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, let \(a_z=|C_z|_d\), and fix a parity class \(\epsilon\in(\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z)^r\) with \(M_\epsilon:=\sum_{z\equiv\epsilon}a_z>0\). For \(c\in\mathbb Z^r\), set
\[
S_c^\epsilon:=\sum_{z\equiv\epsilon}a_za_{2c-z},\qquad
b_c^\epsilon:=S_c^\epsilon/M_\epsilon.
\]
For \(S_c^\epsilon>0\), let \(g_z\) be the centroid of every positive-volume contributing fiber and set
\[
q_c^\epsilon:=\frac1{S_c^\epsilon}\sum_{z\equiv\epsilon}a_za_{2c-z}\frac{g_z+g_{2c-z}}2.
\]
Prove
\[
q_c^\epsilon\in\mathsf M_{b_c^\epsilon}(C_c),\qquad
\sum_cb_c^\epsilon=M_\epsilon.
\]
Consequently the atomic graph measure
\[
\beta_\epsilon:=\sum_{c:S_c^\epsilon>0}b_c^\epsilon\delta_{(c,q_c^\epsilon)}
\]
has mass \(M_\epsilon\) and every ambient closed halfspace \(H\) satisfies
\[
\mu_C(H)\ge\gamma_d\beta_\epsilon(H).
\]

parity-midpoint-domination.statement:
For the mixed-volume measure \(\mu\) of a convex body \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\), prove a compact parity-midpoint halfspace-domination theorem containing both of the following constructions.

First, for every positive finite Borel measure \(\rho\) carried by \(C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)\), average independent same-parity midpoints over all parity classes with the normalization that gives total mass \(|\rho|/2\). Prove that the resulting measure is carried by the same mixed-integer set, is dominated by \(\rho\) on every closed halfspace, and has the same normalized barycenter.

Second, for the original mixed-volume measure, form the unnormalized ordered off-diagonal same-parity midpoint measure \(\eta^\circ\). Prove its exact mass
\[
Q^\circ=\sum_rW_r^2-\sum_z w_z^2
\ge 2^{-n}W^2-MW,
\qquad M:=\max_z w_z,
\]
and the transfer inequality
\[
\eta^\circ(H)\le2W\mu(H)
\]
for every closed halfspace \(H\). State the heavy-fiber alternative and the exact conditional implication from a \(\kappa\)-deep point of \(\eta^\circ\) to a \((\kappa/4)2^{-n}W\) mixed-depth point under \(M<2^{-n-1}W\).

parity-single-level-concentration.relation_to_goal:
For a convex body \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\), the fiber-volume root
\(g(z)=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z)^{1/d}\) is concave on the compact base
projection and
\[
W=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}g(z)^d
\]
is its total mixed-integer volume.  The registered inequality therefore
selects one positive root-volume level carrying at least
\(2^{-n-1}W\) in the product ``level height times lattice count.''  This
has the correct \(2^{-n}\) scale up to one absolute factor and replaces the
unproved dyadic/thick-thin layer selection in the attachment.

The lemma does not itself produce a point of mixed halfspace depth.  A later
step must convert the selected lattice-convex level set into one compatible
affine, simplex, or symmetric-box fiber-depth certificate.  In base
dimension two, a constant-fraction lattice-triangle extraction is a
candidate terminal bridge; in arbitrary dimension that extraction remains
open.  Thus this subgoal is a non-final structural dependency and must have
\(\texttt{target_match: null}\).
parity-single-level-concentration.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a
nonempty compact convex set, and let \(g:P\to[0,\infty)\) be concave.
Put
\[
D:=P\cap\mathbb Z^n,
\qquad
W:=\sum_{z\in D}g(z)^d,
\]
and assume \(W>0\).  For \(s>0\), define
\[
N(s):=\#\{z\in D:g(z)\ge s\},
\qquad
M:=\max_{s>0}s^dN(s).
\]
Prove
\[
M\ge 2^{-n-1}W.
\]

partial-affine-section-depth-lift.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let \(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\) be a convex body of positive mixed mass, write \(C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}\), and let \(\delta_C(z,x)\) denote absolute halfspace depth in the fiber \(C_z\). For an affine map \(s:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^d\), define
\[
q_s(z):=
\begin{cases}
\delta_C(z,s(z)),&(z,s(z))\in C,\\
0,&(z,s(z))\notin C,
\end{cases}
\qquad Q_C(s):=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}q_s(z).
\]
Prove that, whenever \(Q_C(s)>0\), there is \(z^\star\in\mathbb Z^n\) with \((z^\star,s(z^\star))\in C\) and
\[
h_{C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}(z^\star,s(z^\star))
\ge 2^{-n}Q_C(s).
\]
Deduce
\[
\max_{p\in C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)}h_S(p)
\ge 2^{-n}\sup_{s\text{ affine}}Q_C(s).
\]
As a folded corollary for \(n=1\), prove the stronger bound
\[
\max_{p\in S}h_S(p)
\ge \frac18\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z}M(z)
\ge \frac{\gamma_d}{8}W,
\qquad
\gamma_d=\left(\frac d{d+1}\right)^d,
\]

partial-symmetry-compression-certificate.relation_to_goal:
This is a new partial-symmetry certificate, not a proposed universal
completion.

The first assertion synchronizes all same-parity scalar pair products at
one integer midpoint with exactly one \(2^{-n}\) factor.  Accepted fact
`aca624dd8874e5a5` instead constructs the full parity-autocorrelation
measure and proves target-fiber capacity; it does not select one midpoint
with the displayed \(A_m/w_m\) ratio.

The second assertion converts geometric overlap after an affine shear and
one unimodular fundamental-cell erosion directly into mixed depth.  Its
loss is the absolute factor \(1/(2e)\), independent of \(n,d,C\).  It is
different from accepted large-projection erosion fact
`0790372855abe672` and affine-selector facts `bb2b5f9519ae23e8` and
`b220933817d23295`: no large projection and no affine selector on the
lattice fibers is assumed.

The next missing implication would be quantitatively explicit.  If one
could prove, under failure of every dyadically heavy primitive slice,
\[
\mathfrak P(C)\geq\eta\,2^{-n}W
\]
for an absolute \(\eta>0\), then the present certificate would give
\[
\sup_{p\in S}h_S(p)\geq\frac{\eta}{2e}\,2^{-n}W.
\]
The complementary slice branch would retain the exact original-mass
threshold through accepted rank-drop fact `314b32bda8a0b01e`.  No such
universal lower bound for \(\mathfrak P(C)\) is asserted here.

Thus the accepted output would isolate the first unsupported step as the
passage from discrete autocorrelation or absence of a heavy primitive
slice to positive sheared eroded pair volume.  It does not restate or
close the locked target.
partial-symmetry-compression-certificate.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, and write
\[
C_z:=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:(z,x)\in C\},\qquad
w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),\qquad
W:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z>0,
\]
\[
S:=C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d).
\]
For \(m\in\mathbb Z^n\), define
\[
A_m:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z\,w_{2m-z}.
\]

Prove the following two assertions.

1. There is \(m\in\mathbb Z^n\) such that
\[
A_m\geq 2^{-n}Ww_m.
\]
In particular, the selected midpoint has \(w_m>0\).

2. Fix arbitrary
\[
L\in\mathbb R^{d\times n},\qquad
m\in\mathbb Z^n,\qquad
U\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z).
\]
Let
\[
T_L(z,x):=(z,x-Lz),\qquad K:=T_L(C),
\]
\[
D_{L,m}:=
\{(v,y):(m+v,y)\in K,\ (m-v,y)\in K\},
\]
\[
Q_U:=U[-1/2,1/2]^n,
\]
and define the base-direction inner erosion
\[
D^-_{L,m,U}:=
\{(v,y):(v+q,y)\in D_{L,m}\text{ for every }q\in Q_U\}.
\]
Put
\[
V_{L,m,U}:=\operatorname{vol}_{n+d}(D^-_{L,m,U}).
\]
If \(V_{L,m,U}>0\), there is a point
\[
p\in C\cap(\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d)
\]
such that
\[
h_S(p)\geq\frac{1}{2e}V_{L,m,U}.
\]
The conclusion must hold for every closed ambient halfspace containing
\(p\), including vertical halfspaces and halfspaces whose boundary carries
positive mixed mass.

Consequently, if
\[
\mathfrak P(C):=
\sup_{\substack{
L\in\mathbb R^{d\times n},\ m\in\mathbb Z^n\\
U\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)}}
V_{L,m,U},
\]
then
\[
\sup_{p\in S}h_S(p)\geq\frac{1}{2e}\mathfrak P(C).
\]

partial-symmetry-rank-drop-dichotomy.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d\) be a convex body, put
\[
w_z:=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_z),\qquad
W:=\sum_{z\in\mathbb Z^n}w_z>0,
\]
and define \(\mathfrak P(C)\) exactly as in accepted fact
`6a9b0f7ac15a23be`: it is the supremum, over real shears \(L\), integer
midpoints \(m\), and \(U\in\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)\), of the
\((n+d)\)-volume of the corresponding symmetric pair body eroded in the
base directions by \(U[-1/2,1/2]^n\).

Prove or disprove that there is an absolute constant \(\eta>0\) such that
every such \(C\) satisfies at least one of:

1. there are \(1\leq r\leq n\), a primitive rank-\((n-r)\) sublattice

   \[
   \sum_{z\in a+L_0}w_z\geq2^{-r}W;
   \]
2. one has
   \[
   \mathfrak P(C)\geq\eta\,2^{-n}W.
   \]

The quantifiers over the shear, midpoint, and unimodular cell inside
\(\mathfrak P\) are unchanged from accepted fact `6a9b0f7ac15a23be`.

phase-deficit-cap-transfer.relation_to_goal:
This abstracts the lossless cap injection underlying accepted large-box fact
`0790372855abe672`. The signed deficit records precisely how far a general
convex body is from the phase-core property. The theorem is useful beyond a
projection box and is not implied by the large-box conclusion, but it is only
a sufficient structural interface and does not settle the locked target.
phase-deficit-cap-transfer.statement:
Let \(n,d\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), \(m=n+d\), let
\(C\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+d}\) be a convex body, let
\(\mathbf q_0=(\mathbf b,\mathbf v_0)\in C\), and let \(0<\alpha<1\). Put
\[
D=(1-\alpha)C+\alpha\mathbf q_0,\qquad
\mathbf p=(1-\alpha)\mathfrak c(C)+\alpha\mathbf q_0,
\]
and assume \(\mathbf p\in\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d\). For
\(\mathbf t\in[0,1)^n\), define the compact phase-anchor set
\[
\mathcal A_{\mathbf t}
=C\cap\left[
\left(\mathbf b+\alpha^{-1}(\mathbb Z^n-\mathbf t)\right)
\times\mathbb R^d
\right].
\]
For an affine functional \(L\) on \(\mathbb R^{n+d}\), define the signed
phase deficit
\[
\Delta_L(\mathbf t)
=L(\mathbf q_0)-\max_{\mathbf q\in\mathcal A_{\mathbf t}}L(\mathbf q),
\]
with \(\Delta_L(\mathbf t)=+\infty\) when
\(\mathcal A_{\mathbf t}=\varnothing\).

Prove the exact cap-transfer inequality
\[
\mu(C\cap\{L\ge0\})
\ge
\operatorname{vol}_m\left\{
\mathbf w\in D:
L(\mathbf w)\ge
\alpha\Delta_L(\{\mathbf w_I\})
\right\},
\]
where \(\{\mathbf w_I\}\in[0,1)^n\) is the canonical fractional part of
the base coordinate and \(\mu\) is mixed-integer volume.

As a corollary, if
\[
\mathbf q_0\in\operatorname{conv}\mathcal A_{\mathbf t}
\quad\text{for every }\mathbf t\in[0,1)^n,
\]
then every closed halfspace \(H\) containing \(\mathbf p\) satisfies
\[
\mu(C\cap H)\ge
\operatorname{vol}_m(D\cap H)
\ge
\left(\frac m{m+1}\right)^m
(1-\alpha)^m\operatorname{vol}_m(C).
\]
Treat empty anchor phases, maximizing-anchor measurability, closed boundaries,
and the distinction between the actual mixed-integer image and its thickened
cell explicitly.

pk-intake-affine-power-inner-cdf.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ be an integer, $0\le r<1$, and let $G$ be the CDF of the probability density $f(t)=dt^{d-1}/(1-r^d)$ on $[r,1]$. Its mean is $m=\frac{d}{d+1}\frac{1-r^{d+1}}{1-r^d}$. With $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, one has $r\le2m-1<1$ and
$$
G(2m-1)\le1-2\gamma_d.
$$

pk-intake-affine-score-moment-partition.relation_to_goal: Realizes exact masses and base moments for intrinsic mixed measure. The result gives no lower bound on centroid halfspace depth and no recursive single-cut construction.
pk-intake-affine-score-moment-partition.statement:
Let $n,d$ be positive integers and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body. Put $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $S=C\cap\Lambda$, and assume $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S\ge 1$. Set $\mu=\mathcal H_q|_S$. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ put $K_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$, and let $P=\{z:w_z=\mathcal H_q(K_z)>0\}$.

Suppose finitely many labeled mass and base moment pairs $(t_i,m_i)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^n$ are feasible: there are $s_{iz}\ge 0$ with $\sum_i s_{iz}=w_z$ for $z\in P$ and $(t_i,m_i)=\sum_{z\in P}s_{iz}(1,z)$ for every label. Discard the labels with $t_i=0$ and index the remaining $k$ labels by $1,\ldots,k$. Fix any vectors $u_i\in\mathbb R^d$ such that $x\mapsto(u_i-u_j)\cdot x$ is nonconstant on each $K_z$ for $z\in P$ whenever $i\ne j$.

There are finite $\theta_i\in\mathbb R^{n+1}$ such that the affine scores $L_i(z,x)=\theta_i\cdot(1,z)+u_i\cdot x$ give closed cells
$$
D_i=C\cap\bigcap_{j\ne i}\{(z,x):L_i(z,x)\ge L_j(z,x)\}.
$$
Each $D_i$ is an ambient convex body cut from $C$ by at most $k-1$ closed halfspaces, and $D_i\cap\Lambda$ has Hausdorff dimension $q$. The cells satisfy
$$
\bigcup_iD_i=C,\qquad
\mu(D_i\cap D_j)=0\quad(i\ne j),\qquad
\left(\mu(D_i),\int_{D_i} z\,d\mu\right)=(t_i,m_i).
$$
In particular they exhaust the mixed measure. The centroid of $\mathcal H_q|_{D_i\cap\Lambda}$ belongs to $D_i$, has base $m_i/t_i$, and lies in $D_i\cap\Lambda$ if that base is integral. Suitable $u_i$ always exist.

pk-intake-all-point-identical-triangle-p.relation_to_goal: Two identical copies of a continuous planar triangle, measured in absolute area at a single marked point. The theorem supplies a bound for one selected pair with a common normal and opposite shifts. The locked conjecture concerns the common ambient halfspace over an entire compatible mixed-integer fiber family.
pk-intake-all-point-identical-triangle-p.statement:
Let $T\subset\mathbb R^2$ be a nondegenerate triangle of area $V$, and let $y\in T$ have barycentric coordinates $A\ge B\ge C$. Write $f_T(y)$ for the infimum of $|T\cap H|$ over closed halfplanes $H$ containing $y$, where $|\cdot|$ denotes area. For $u\ne0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, set
$$
P_T(y;u,t)=|T\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y+t\}|+
           |T\cap\{x:u\cdot x\ge u\cdot y-t\}|.
$$
Then $P_T(y;u,t)\ge 8BCV$ for every $u\ne0$ and $t\in\mathbb R$, and
$$
\min_{u\ne0,\ t\in\mathbb R}P_T(y;u,t)=8BCV=2f_T(y).
$$
The minimum is attained at shift zero, including when $y\in\partial T$.

pk-intake-arithmetic-power-sum-concavity.relation_to_goal: A scalar unit-step inequality at actual nodes, for arbitrary real d≥1.
pk-intake-arithmetic-power-sum-concavity.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be real and $\rho>0$. For integers $m\ge0$ put $A_m=\sum_{j=0}^m(\rho+j)^d$. The sequence $(A_m^{1/(d+1)})_{m\ge0}$ is concave at every integer midpoint $m\ge1$. In particular, for $S_d(q)=\sum_{j\ge0}(q-j)_+^d$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$, every real $q>1$ satisfies
$$
S_d(q+1)^{1/(d+1)}+S_d(q-1)^{1/(d+1)}\le 2S_d(q)^{1/(d+1)}.
$$
For each fixed $d$ the exponent $1/(d+1)$ is the largest positive exponent that works uniformly over the sequences $A_m$.

pk-intake-canonical-fiber-energy-boundar.relation_to_goal: Joint energy on fiber-interior marks of an ordinary finite canonical hull, including sampled bases on its relative boundary. The counterexample separates the general ambient-body boundary issue from positivity of a chart.
pk-intake-canonical-fiber-energy-boundar.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, let each $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$ be a convex body, and assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subset K_p$ whenever $\lambda_z\ge0$, $\sum_z\lambda_z=1$, and $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$. Set $Q=\operatorname{conv}P$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$. For the positive attained energy
$E_K(y)=\min_a\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over denominators positive on $K$, put $F(z,x)=E_{C_z}(x)^{1/d}$ on $\Omega_C=\{(z,x):z\in Q,\ x\in\operatorname{int}C_z\}$.

Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$, let $a_y$ be the optimizer at this mark in $K_p$, and put $F_0=F(p,y)$. The function $F$ is locally Lipschitz relative to $\operatorname{aff}(Q)\times\mathbb R^d$ on its domain near $(p,y)$, and there is a finite $B\in\operatorname{span}(Q-Q)$ such that
$$
F(z,x)\le F_0\left[1+B\cdot(z-p)+\frac{d+1}{d}a_y\cdot(x-y)\right]\qquad((z,x)\in\Omega_C).
$$
Every supergradient at $(p,y)$ has continuous component $\frac{d+1}{d}F_0a_y$. The associated affine chart
$$
L(z,x)=1+a_y\cdot(x-y)+\frac{d}{d+1}B\cdot(z-p)
$$
is at least $1/(d+1)$ on $C$ and strictly greater on $\Omega_C$. The base point $p$ may lie on the relative boundary of $Q$. For arbitrary compact convex ambient bodies a finite boundary-base energy supergradient can fail, even with full-dimensional ball fibers.

pk-intake-canonical-fibers-hausdorff-lip.relation_to_goal: Finite canonical hulls over arbitrary real sampled bases, with no anchored inclusion or lattice assumptions.
pk-intake-canonical-fibers-hausdorff-lip.statement:
Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, with a compact convex body $K_p\subset\mathbb R^d$ of nonempty interior for every $p\in P$, where $d\ge1$. Let $Q=\operatorname{conv}P$ and $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{p\in P}(\{p\}\times K_p)$. For every $z\in Q$ let $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$. The fibers $C_z$ are convex bodies with a uniform positive inradius. If $h_K(u)=\max_{x\in K}u\cdot x$, then
$$
h_{C_z}(u)=\max_{\substack{\lambda_p\ge0,\ \sum_p\lambda_p=1\\ \sum_p\lambda_p p=z}}
\sum_p\lambda_p h_{K_p}(u).
$$
There is a finite constant $L$ depending on the given family such that $d_H(C_z,C_{z'})\le L\|z-z'\|$ for all $z,z'\in Q$, including its relative boundary. In particular, for each $y\in\operatorname{int}C_z$, the fibers at all sufficiently close bases in $Q$ contain a common ball centered at $y$.

pk-intake-capped-integer-first-moment.relation_to_goal: An exact one-sided first-moment maximization under an integer site capacity.
pk-intake-capped-integer-first-moment.statement:
Let $h\in\mathbb Z$, $m>0$, and let $(a_i)_{i\le h}$ be finitely supported with $0\le a_i\le m$ and total mass $A$. Write $A=qm+u$ with $q\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ and $0\le u<m$. The largest possible first moment for these $h,m,A$ is
$$
hA-\frac{mq(q-1)}2-qu
=hA-\frac{A^2}{2m}+\frac A2-\frac{u(m-u)}{2m}.
$$
It is attained by putting mass $m$ at $h,h-1,\ldots,h-q+1$, mass $u$ at $h-q$, and zero elsewhere. In particular the first moment is at most $hA-A^2/(2m)+A/2$.

pk-intake-centroid-graph-surplus-first-o.relation_to_goal: This gives optimal first-order control of one fiber-centroid shift and of the width of a threshold-qualified centroid hull section. It yields no bound for the global mixed halfspace depth and no weighted Helly assertion. The constants concern vanishing surplus, with d fixed.
pk-intake-centroid-graph-surplus-first-o.statement:
Let $n,d\ge1$ and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body. For $z\in\mathbb Z^n$ write $K_z=\{y:(z,y)\in C\}$ and let $g_z$ be its volume centroid when $|K_z|>0$. Fix an integer base $w$ with $|K_w|>0$. For any finite convex representation
$$
(w,x)=\sum_i\lambda_i(z_i,g_{z_i}),\qquad
\lambda_i>0,\quad \sum_i\lambda_i=1,\quad |K_{z_i}|>0,
$$
set $a=(\sum_i\lambda_i|K_{z_i}|^{1/d})^d$ and $\delta=1-a/|K_w|\in[0,1)$. For a nonzero linear functional $u$ on $\mathbb R^d$ let $W=\max_{K_w}u-\min_{K_w}u$. Then
$$
\frac{|u(x-g_w)|}{W}
\le \min\left\{\delta,\ \frac{d}{d+1}\frac{\delta}{1-\delta},\ \frac{d}{d+1}\right\}.
$$
For $0\le\varepsilon<1$, let $S_\varepsilon(w)$ be the set of all $x$ admitting such a representation with $a\ge (1-\varepsilon)|K_w|$. The width of $u(S_\varepsilon(w))$ is at most $\frac{\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon}W$.

For every $d\ge1$ and $0<\delta<1$, an actual body with $n=1$, three integer fibers, and a representation at $w=0$ attains
$$
\frac{u(x-g_w)}{W}=\frac{d}{d+1}\frac{\delta(1-\delta^{1/d})}{1-\delta}.
$$
Consequently the coefficient $d/(d+1)$ is optimal to first order as $\delta\downarrow0$, even for such bodies. For every $d\ge1$ and $0<\varepsilon<1$, an actual body with $n=2$, five integer fibers, and $w=0$ has width $\varepsilon W$ for $u(S_\varepsilon(0))$. Thus the width coefficient one is optimal to first order as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$.

pk-intake-compact-double-knot-reduction.relation_to_goal: Scalar finite-sum variational reduction on a compact domain with a retained positive cutoff edge. Unrestricted small-slope exclusion, comparisons among the knots, and geometric depth are separate.
pk-intake-compact-double-knot-reduction.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$. Write $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$, $t=1/(d+1)$, and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. For $a>0$, $0\le\beta\le at$, and $h\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ put $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$, and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$. Define $E(u,r)=d^d u^{d-1}(r-du)_+$ when $u,r>0$ and $E(u,0)=0$ for all real $u$. The finite deficit is
$$
D(a,\beta)=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d-\sum_{h\ge0}\bigl[E(q_h,r_h)+E(p_h,r_h)\bigr].
$$

For every $0<\epsilon\le1$, let $P_\epsilon=\{(a,\beta):\epsilon\le a\le1,\ 0\le\beta\le at\}$. The deficit is continuous there and its maximum is attained. Let $K_\epsilon$ consist of the points in $P_\epsilon$ of the form
$$
a=\frac{t(H+J+1)}{H(2J+1)},\qquad
\beta=\frac{t(H-J)}{dH(2J+1)},
\qquad H,J\in\mathbb Z,\quad H\ge1,\quad 0\le J\le H\le(2d+1)J+d.
$$
Then $K_\epsilon$ is finite, includes boundary coincidences, and
$$
\max_{(a,\beta)\in P_\epsilon}D(a,\beta)
=\max\left(\{0,\ \max_{0\le\beta\le\epsilon t}D(\epsilon,\beta)\}
      \cup\{D(a,\beta):(a,\beta)\in K_\epsilon\}\right).
$$
Throughout the domain $a>0$, $0\le\beta\le at$, the deficit is nonpositive on $\beta=0$, on $\beta=at$, and for $a\ge1$.

pk-intake-concave-root-tail-concavity.relation_to_goal: A scalar positive-sequence theorem on actual tail indices.
pk-intake-concave-root-tail-concavity.statement: Let $d\ge1$ be real, let $\ell\le r$ be integers, and let $a_\ell,\ldots,a_r>0$ have concave $d$th roots, meaning the successive differences of $a_i^{1/d}$ are nonincreasing. Set $F_i=\sum_{j=i}^r a_j$. Then $(F_i^{1/(d+1)})_{i=\ell}^r$ is concave on its actual indices. The exponent is the largest positive exponent that works for every such sequence at fixed $d$.

pk-intake-continuous-anchored-support-sl.relation_to_goal: A support-selection result for fixed finite affine base coordinates and an anchored inclusion. The affine rank is unrestricted. The continuity assertion concerns the support right-hand sides for a fixed base matrix. The result supplies a geometric input to mixed-integer erosion constructions without a halfspace-depth bound.
pk-intake-continuous-anchored-support-sl.statement:
Let $n\ge0$ and $d\ge1$ be integers. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be nonempty and finite, fix $p\in P$, and for each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, compact, and convex. Assume the anchored Minkowski inclusion
$$
\sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p
\quad\text{whenever}\quad
\lambda_z\ge0,\qquad \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z=1,\qquad \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z z=p .
\tag{1}
$$
Use the given Euclidean base coordinates. The affine rank $r=\dim\operatorname{span}(P-p)$ may be any integer from $0$ to $n$. Write $h_z(u)=\max_{x\in K_z}u\cdot x$. For every $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ the inequalities
$$
h_z(u)\le h_p(u)+A\cdot(z-p)\qquad(z\in P)
\tag{2}
$$
have a unique minimum-Euclidean-norm solution $A_p(u)$. It lies in $\operatorname{span}(P-p)$, and the map $u\mapsto A_p(u)$ is continuous and bounded. The affine function $z\mapsto h_p(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)$ yields a supporting inequality $u\cdot x\le h_p(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)$ on $\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$, with equality at every point of the $u$-supporting face of $\{p\}\times K_p$.

pk-intake-effective-cap-count-profile.relation_to_goal: Ordinary continuous cap volumes. The result may be used in the affine hull of one positive-dimensional mixed fiber. A whole trace gives a mass-V term directly, and empty traces contribute zero. It gives no common lattice point or global trimming or summation rule.
pk-intake-effective-cap-count-profile.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V$, with $D\ge1$. Let $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ be proper closed halfspaces covering $K$, where $m\ge1$, and write $A_i=|K\cap H_i|$. Put $\gamma_0=1$ and $\gamma_q=(q/(q+1))^q$ for integers $q\ge1$. For any fixed inclusion-minimal subcover indexed by $I$, let $j=|I|$ and let $\rho$ be the rank of its normals. For every $\alpha\ge0$,
$$
\sum_{i\in I}(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_{\min(\rho,j-1)}}\ge V,
\qquad x_+=\max(x,0).
$$
Consequently, with $s=\min(D,m-1)$,
$$
\sum_{i=1}^m(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_s}\ge V
\quad(\alpha\ge0),
\qquad
\sum_{i=1}^m A_i-V\ge (m-1/\gamma_s)\min_i A_i .
$$
For each pair $(D,m)$, $\gamma_s$ is the largest constant that can replace it in the all-cover positive-part profile.

pk-intake-entropy-balanced-mass-equality.relation_to_goal: Compares scalar finite-base capacities. Dominated escort mass is given by the separate factor c.
pk-intake-entropy-balanced-mass-equality.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine Euclidean space, with masses $m_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv} P$ and $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$. Fix $N>0$ and $p\in Q$. Let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ with $p\in\operatorname{relint} F_p$, and write $P_p=P\cap F_p$ and $V_p=\operatorname{span}(F_p-p)$. Set
$$
L_z(\alpha)=1+\alpha\cdot(z-p),\qquad
E_p=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in V_p\\L_z(\alpha)>0\ (z\in P_p)}}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}.
$$

Let $\alpha_p$ be the unique relative minimizer and $M_p=\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z$. For $p\in Q$ define
$$
T_p=\max_{\substack{0\le q_z\le m_z\\\sum_{z\in P}q_z(z-p)=0}}\sum_{z\in P}q_z,\qquad
D_p=\min_{H\ni p}\sum_{z\in P\cap H}m_z,
$$
where $H$ ranges over closed affine halfspaces in $\operatorname{aff} Q$, with the whole-space trace allowed, including rank zero. The capacity and the halfspace depth are unchanged on restriction to $P_p$ in $\operatorname{aff}F_p$. With $a$ ranging over $\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$,
$$
T_p=\inf_a\sum_{z\in P}m_z(1+a\cdot(z-p))_+,\qquad
E_p\ge T_p\ge D_p .
$$
Writing $b_N(L)=L^{-N}-(1-N(L-1))_+$ for $L>0$, one has
$$
E_p-T_p\ge\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z b_N(L_z(\alpha_p)),\qquad
E_p=T_p\ \Longleftrightarrow\ p=M_p^{-1}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z z .
$$
At equality $E_p=T_p=M_p$.

The escort masses $e_z=m_z L_z(\alpha_p)^{-N-1}$ on $P_p$ and zero off $P_p$ are dominated by the $m_z$ exactly when $\alpha_p=0$. The largest scalar $c\ge0$ with $c e_z\le m_z$ for all $z$ is $c=\min_{z\in P_p}L_z(\alpha_p)^{N+1}$. The resulting dominated row has total mass $cE_p$ and mean $p$. On the whole of $Q$, $E_p\le M$ with equality exactly at the original weighted base mean. If this mean is occupied and the compatible-fiber assumptions of the face-attainment result hold with $m_z=|K_z|$, its escort-selected continuous coordinate equals the original volume-weighted fiber centroid.

pk-intake-entropy-face-attainment-dual.relation_to_goal: Finite weighted bases and real N>0. Fiber compatibility gives membership of the centroid combination in its fiber.
pk-intake-entropy-face-attainment-dual.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in an affine Euclidean space, with masses $m_z>0$ for $z\in P$, and put $Q=\operatorname{conv} P$ and $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$. Fix $N>0$ and $p\in Q$. Let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ with $p\in\operatorname{relint} F_p$, and write $P_p=P\cap F_p$ and $V_p=\operatorname{span}(F_p-p)$. Set
$$
L_z(\alpha)=1+\alpha\cdot(z-p),\qquad
E_p=\inf_{\substack{\alpha\in V_p\\L_z(\alpha)>0\ (z\in P_p)}}\sum_{z\in P_p}m_z L_z(\alpha)^{-N}.
$$

The infimum is attained at a unique $\alpha_p$. Its value is also the infimum of the analogous sum over $P$ with $\alpha\in\operatorname{span}(Q-p)$ and all denominators positive. This latter infimum is attained exactly when $F_p=Q$. In particular a singleton face $F_p=\{p\}$ gives $E_p=m_p$.

Let $e_z=m_zL_z(\alpha_p)^{-N-1}$ on $P_p$, and $e_z=0$ off $P_p$. Then $\sum_{z\in P}e_z=E_p$ and $\sum_{z\in P}e_z z=E_p p$. With $s=N/(N+1)$,
$$
E_p=\max_{\substack{\lambda_z\ge0,\ \sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z=1\\\sum_{z\in P}\lambda_z z=p}}
\left(\sum_{z\in P}m_z^{1/(N+1)}\lambda_z^s\right)^{N+1},
$$
and the unique maximizer is $\lambda_z=e_z/E_p$. In particular $E_p^{1/(N+1)}$ is concave on $Q$. If $\pi_z=m_z/M$ and $D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi)=(s-1)^{-1}\log\sum_z\lambda_z^s\pi_z^{1-s}$, then $E_p/M=\exp(-\min_\lambda D_s(\lambda\Vert\pi))$, over the same constraint set.

If $p\in P$ and $m_z$ are volumes of positive-volume compact convex $d$-fibers $K_z$ with centroids $g_z$, assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p$ for the displayed maximizing row (as for fibers of a convex body). Then $\sum_z\lambda_z g_z\in\operatorname{int}K_p$.

pk-intake-entropy-lattice-maximum-equali.relation_to_goal: Lattice-complete finite weighted supports. The conclusion is about the maximum of a scalar base energy.
pk-intake-entropy-lattice-maximum-equali.statement:
Let $\Lambda=c+L$ be an affine lattice, and let $P$ be a nonempty finite set with $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\Lambda$. Give every $z\in P$ mass $m_z>0$, put $M=\sum_{z\in P}m_z$, and let $k$ be the number of occupied cosets modulo $2L$. For $N>0$ let $E_p$ be the power-entropy energy defined in the face-attainment result, using the minimal face of $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ at each $p\in P$. Then
$$
\max_{p\in P}E_p\ge M/k,\qquad
\max_{p\in P}E_p=M/k
\ \Longleftrightarrow\
P\text{ consists of exactly }k\text{ vertices, all with mass }M/k.
$$
If $\operatorname{rank}L\le n$, the maximum is at least $M/2^n$, with equality exactly when $k=2^n$ and the same equal-vertex condition holds. Equal masses on $\{0,1\}^n$ attain this bound.

pk-intake-equal-endpoint-actual-mixed-ce.relation_to_goal: Strict normalized depth above the sharp three-fiber threshold at the actual mixed centroid with one integer coordinate and equal endpoint masses.
pk-intake-equal-endpoint-actual-mixed-ce.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be an integer, and let $A,K,B\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies of volumes $v,k,v>0$ with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$. Let $\mu$ be the sum of the $d$-volumes on the integer fibers $A,K,B$ at bases $-1,0,1$ of their lifted convex hull. The actual mixed centroid is

$$
Y=\left(0,\frac{v g_A+k g_K+v g_B}{k+2v}\right),
$$

where $g_A,g_K,g_B$ are the uniform-volume centroids. It lies in $\lbrace 0\rbrace\times\operatorname{int}K$. Write $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, $A_d=1/\Gamma_d$, and let the positive constant $\varepsilon_d$ be

$$
\varepsilon_d=\frac{d}{d+1}\left[2+(1+1/d)(1+A_d/3)
-2(1+1/(2d))^{d+1}-2(1-(4A_d/3-1)/(2d))_+^{d+1}\right],
$$

with $t_+=\max(t,0)$. The raw depth at $Y$, the infimum of $\mu(H)$ over closed ambient halfspaces containing $Y$, is at least

$$
\frac{3\Gamma_d}{4}(k+v)+
\min\left(\frac{3\Gamma_d^2\varepsilon_d k}{4\cdot3^d},
               (1-3\Gamma_d/4)(k+v)\right).
$$

In particular it is strictly greater than $(3\Gamma_d/4)(k+v)\ge(\Gamma_d/2)(k+2v)$. The same conclusion holds in any convex body whose only positive $d$-volume integer fibers are those three fibers; any other integer fibers of zero $d$-volume do not affect $\mu$.

pk-intake-explicit-diagonal-small-slope-.relation_to_goal: A fixed-dimension explicit slope range of strictly negative scalar diagonal-envelope deficit, uniform over the allowed tilt interval.
pk-intake-explicit-diagonal-small-slope-.statement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$ and put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. For $a>0$, $0\le\beta\le at$ and $h\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$, set $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$ and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$, where $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. The diagonal-envelope deficit is
$$
D(a,\beta)=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d
-d^d\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}
  \left[q_h^{d-1}(r_h-dq_h)_++p_h^{d-1}(r_h-dp_h)_+\right].
$$
Both sums have only finitely many nonzero terms. Whenever $r_h>0$, one has $q_h\ge tr_h>0$ and $p_h\ge t>0$.

With the constants $C_d$ and $K_d$ of the uniform deficit expansion, define
$$
\varepsilon_d=\min\left\{\frac1{2d},\frac1{4[C_d+(d+1)K_d^2]}\right\}.
$$
For every $0<a\le1/(2d)$ and $0\le\beta\le at$,
$$
\frac{D(a,\beta)}{\Gamma}\le -\frac12+[C_d+(d+1)K_d^2]a.
$$
In particular $D(a,\beta)\le-\Gamma/4$ for all $0<a\le\varepsilon_d$ and $0\le\beta\le at$.

pk-intake-exterior-contact-dimension-dro.relation_to_goal: Finite closed covers with a common exterior or boundary contact for one continuous body. The mixed statement tests one actual fiber at a time.
pk-intake-exterior-contact-dimension-dro.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body, and let $y\notin\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose finitely many proper closed halfspaces $H_i$ cover $\mathbb R^d$ and all their boundary hyperplanes contain $y$. Then
$$
\max_i |K\cap H_i|\ge\gamma_{d-1}|K|,
\qquad \gamma_j=\left(\frac{j}{j+1}\right)^j\ (j\ge1),\quad \gamma_0=1.
$$
For each $d$ the constant is attained both for some $y\notin K$ and for some $y\in\partial K$. For $d\ge2$ the constant also remains the infimum for each contact type when the normals span $\mathbb R^d$, equivalently when $y$ is the unique common point of their boundaries.

pk-intake-exterior-origin-radial-gauge.relation_to_goal: Convexity of a radial gauge for a compactly supported inverse-power density, including exterior origins.
pk-intake-exterior-origin-radial-gauge.statement:
Let $p\ge1$, and let $f$ be a bounded nonnegative upper-semicontinuous function of compact support on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space. Assume $\{f>0\}$ has nonempty interior and the extended function $f^{-1/(p+1)}$, with value $+\infty$ where $f=0$, is convex. For $x\ne0$ put $I_p(x)=\int_0^\infty t^{p-1}f(tx)\,dt$. Then
$$
U_p=\{0\}\cup\{x\ne0:I_p(x)\ge1\}
$$
is compact and convex. Its gauge is $I_p(x)^{-1/p}$ for $x\ne0$, interpreted as $+\infty$ if $I_p(x)=0$, and is zero at the origin. If $f$ is positive on a neighborhood of the origin, $U_p$ is a convex body with the origin in its interior.

pk-intake-finite-capacity-allocation-ext.relation_to_goal: An extreme-point and dual certificate for fractional sites in a finite base allocation.
pk-intake-finite-capacity-allocation-ext.statement:
Let $P\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be finite, with capacities $a_z>0$ for $z\in P$. Fix a mass $m\ge0$ and a vector $g\in\mathbb R^n$, and assume
$$
Q=\{b:0\le b_z\le a_z,\ \sum_{z\in P}b_z=m,\ \sum_{z\in P}z b_z=mg\}
$$
is nonempty. A point of $Q$ is extreme exactly when the columns $(1,z)$ at its partially filled sites $0<b_z<a_z$ are linearly independent. Every linear cost $\sum_z c_zb_z$ has an extreme minimizer, and this minimizer has at most $\operatorname{rank}((1,z)_{z\in P})\le n+1$ partially filled sites.

There are a scalar $\lambda$ and vector $v\in\mathbb R^n$ such that the minimum value is
$$
\lambda m+v\cdot(mg)+\sum_{z\in P}a_z\min(0,c_z-\lambda-v\cdot z).
$$
For this pair a feasible $b$ is optimal exactly when $b_z=a_z$ at each strict negative reduced cost $c_z-\lambda-v\cdot z$ and $b_z=0$ at each strict positive one. If $c_z=\|z-g\|_2^2$ and $m>0$, the reduced cost is the squared distance from $g+v/2$ minus a nonnegative squared radius. Every optimizer thus fills the strict interior sites of the corresponding closed ball, leaves its exterior sites empty, and can be fractional only on its sphere.

pk-intake-finite-global-cut-radial-loss.relation_to_goal: First losses under actual relative convex-body erosions on a fixed compatible finite lattice base, including fixed supporting traces.
pk-intake-finite-global-cut-radial-loss.statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior. Assume $\sum_z\lambda_z K_z\subseteq K_p$ whenever $\lambda_z\ge0$, $\sum_z\lambda_z=1$, and $\sum_z\lambda_z z=p\in P$. Put $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$ and $h_z=h_{K_z}$.

A finite global-cut action on $C$ uses a nonempty finite index set $I$. For each $i\in I$, its function $\ell_i(u,z)$ is continuous in $u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}$ and affine in $z\in\operatorname{aff}(P)$, with $\ell_i(u,z)\ge h_z(u)$ on $P$. Its field $V_i(u,z,x)$ is jointly continuous and nonnegative on $\mathbb S^{d-1}\times C$ and convex in $(z,x)$ on $C$ for each fixed $u$. Fields satisfying these assumptions on a larger common convex domain can be restricted to $C$. For $\varepsilon\ge0$ define
$$
C_\varepsilon=C\cap
\bigcap_{i\in I,\;u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}
\{(z,x):u\cdot x+\varepsilon V_i(u,z,x)\le\ell_i(u,z)\}.
$$
Then $C_0=C$, and for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$, $C_\varepsilon$ is a nested compact convex body in $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$. Its projection is $\operatorname{conv}(P)$, its integer fibers $K_z(\varepsilon)=(C_\varepsilon)_z$ have nonempty interior exactly for $z\in P$, and it has no other integer fibers. The deformed fibers satisfy all the same anchored Minkowski inclusions.

At a regular $x\in\partial K_z$, with unique outward unit normal $\nu_z(x)$, define
$$
v_z(x)=\max\Bigl(\{V_i(\nu_z(x),z,x):i\in I,\ \ell_i(\nu_z(x),z)=h_z(\nu_z(x))\}\cup\{0\}\Bigr).
$$
About each fixed $o_z\in\operatorname{int}K_z$, let $s_\varepsilon(x)$ be the fractional radial loss, so the new endpoint on the ray through $x$ is $o_z+(1-s_\varepsilon(x))(x-o_z)$. The ratios $s_\varepsilon(x)/\varepsilon$ are uniformly bounded in $x\in\partial K_z$ and, at each regular $x$, tend to $v_z(x)/[\nu_z(x)\cdot(x-o_z)]$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$. Thus
$$
|K_z|-|K_z(\varepsilon)|=\varepsilon\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS+o(\varepsilon),
\qquad dS=d\mathcal H^{d-1}.
$$

Let $\mu_\varepsilon(H)=\sum_{z\in P}|K_z(\varepsilon)\cap H_z|$, where $H_z=\{x:(z,x)\in H\}$ for a fixed closed ambient halfspace $H$. On $\partial K_z$, let $\kappa_{z,H}$ be $1$ if $K_z\subseteq H_z$, $0$ if $\operatorname{int}K_z\cap H_z=\varnothing$, and $\mathbf1_{\operatorname{int}H_z}$ otherwise. The first case includes an inside supporting cut and a pure-base cut whose boundary contains the whole fiber. The second includes an outside supporting trace, even when that trace has positive surface measure. Then
$$
\mu_0(H)-\mu_\varepsilon(H)=\varepsilon L(H)+o(\varepsilon),
\qquad L(H)=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}\kappa_{z,H}v_z\,dS.
$$
The first total loss is $D=\sum_{z\in P}\int_{\partial K_z}v_z\,dS$. The remainders can be taken uniformly on each fixed finite cap list. For $d=1$, $dS$ is counting measure on the two endpoints.

pk-intake-finite-global-cut-speed-additi.relation_to_goal: Finite nonnegative addition of actual global-cut speeds on one common family, with their fixed linear responses.
pk-intake-finite-global-cut-speed-additi.statement:
On one common family $P,(K_z)_{z\in P},C$ as in the finite global-cut radial loss lemma, let $a=1,\ldots,N$, $N\ge1$, index finite global-cut actions with fields $V_{ai}$ and baselines $\ell_{ai}$. For any fixed coefficients $\alpha_a\ge0$, one finite global-cut action on $C$ has inward speeds
$$
v_{\alpha,z}(x)=\sum_{a=1}^N\alpha_a v_{a,z}(x)
$$
at every regular point $x$ of every original measured boundary $\partial K_z$. It has first total loss $D_\alpha=\sum_a\alpha_a D_a$ and, for every fixed closed ambient halfspace $H$, first cap loss $L_\alpha(H)=\sum_a\alpha_a L_a(H)$, with uniform little-o remainders on each fixed finite cap list. In particular it gives exactly the same combination of the first response rows $L_a(H)-\beta D_a$ for any fixed level $\beta$, and of the integrals of the speeds against any fixed bounded Borel boundary weights. If every $\alpha_a=0$, the constructed action is identically $C$ for all $\varepsilon\ge0$. All actions, including the constructed one, have zero-parameter body exactly $C$. The speeds and their finite linear response vectors therefore form algebraic cones under finite nonnegative combinations.

pk-intake-general-projective-volume-marg.relation_to_goal: Continuous ordinary-volume pushforward. The change of variables makes no assertion about a mixed-integer measure or a lattice-preserving map.
pk-intake-general-projective-volume-marg.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body with affine coordinates $(v,t,y)$, where $v\in\mathbb R^r$, $1\le r\le D-1$, $y\in\mathbb R^{D-r-1}$, and $t\ge0$ on $K$. Write $J>0$ for the constant volume Jacobian of these coordinates. The pushforward of $D$-volume on $K\cap\{t>0\}$ under $z=v/t$ has bounded integrable density
$$
F(z)=J\int_0^\infty\int_{\mathbb R^{D-r-1}}\mathbf1_K(tz,t,y)t^r\,dy\,dt
    =J\int_0^\infty\int_{\mathbb R^{D-r-1}}\mathbf1_\Omega(z,s,w)s^{-(D+1)}\,dw\,ds,
$$
where $\Omega=\{(z,s,w):s>0,\ (z/s,1/s,w/s)\in K\}$. The set $\{F>0\}$ is convex and full-dimensional, and $F^{-1/(r+1)}$ is convex on it. Its boundary may be discarded without changing the measure. The total mass is $|K|$, and any cap on $K$ with margin $a\cdot v+bt$ has exactly the mass of $\{z:a\cdot z+b\ge0\}$ under $F(z)\,dz$.

pk-intake-hereditary-depth-distal-cap-tr.relation_to_goal: The abstract measure must have null hyperplanes and the stated hereditary depth property. Ordinary volume supplies this property on each positive-volume convex restriction, including restrictions within a single continuous fiber. The locked mixed-integer target would require depth for the original mixed measure and uniform control across lattice fibers.
pk-intake-hereditary-depth-distal-cap-tr.statement:
Let $D\ge1$, let $\mu$ be a finite nonnegative Borel measure on $\mathbb{R}^D$ with convex support $K=\operatorname{supp}\mu$, and suppose every affine hyperplane has zero $\mu$-mass. Assume there is a fixed $g>0$ such that every closed convex subset $L\subseteq K$ of positive $\mu$-mass contains a point $y$ satisfying $\mu(L\cap H)\ge g\mu(L)$ for every closed halfspace $H$ containing $y$.

Let $H_1,\ldots,H_m$ be a finite cover of $K$ by closed halfspaces with nonzero normals, with $m\ge1$, and let $A_i=\mu(H_i)$. For every $\alpha\ge0$,
$$
\mu(K)\le\sum_{i=1}^m(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{g},
\qquad x_+=\max\{x,0\}.
\tag{1}
$$

For ordinary volume on a convex body $K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^D$, write $V=\operatorname{vol}_D(K)$ and $\gamma_D=(D/(D+1))^D$. Then (1) holds with $g=\gamma_D$ and $A_i=\operatorname{vol}_D(K\cap H_i)$. In particular, for $a=\min_i A_i$,
$$
\sum_{i=1}^m A_i-V\ge(m-1/\gamma_D)a.
\tag{2}
$$
Arrange the cap masses in decreasing order and append zeros if $m<3$. For $D\ge2$,
$$
A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}+(1/\gamma_D-2)A_{(3)}\ge V,
\tag{3}
$$
where $0<1/\gamma_D-2<1$. For $D=1$, $A_{(1)}+A_{(2)}\ge V$.

pk-intake-homothetic-middle-centroid-sur.relation_to_goal: A pointwise result for one integer coordinate and three actual homothetic positive fibers in the stated radius strip.
pk-intake-homothetic-middle-centroid-sur.statement:
Let $d\ge 2$ and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V$ and centroid zero. The only positive-volume integer fibers of a convex body in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ are $A=a+rK$, $B=b+RK$, and $C=c+sK$ at bases $-1,0,1$, respectively, with $r,R,s>0$ and $(A+C)/2\subseteq B$. Write $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $M=V(r^d+R^d+s^d)$. Raw mass means the sum of the $d$-dimensional volumes of the traces on the actual integer fibers. Label the endpoints so that $r\le s$, and assume $s<R$ and $R^d<r^d+s^d$. For every closed ambient halfspace $H$ containing $(0,b)$, its raw mass satisfies
$$
\mu(H)\ge V\left[\gamma_dR^d+\frac{(r-2(R-s))^d}{2}\right]
\ge \frac{\gamma_d M}{2}+\frac{1-2\gamma_d}{4}V(r^d+s^d-R^d)
>\frac{\gamma_d M}{2}.
$$

pk-intake-independent-normal-strict-cap-.relation_to_goal: Gives strictness for fixed independent-normal ordinary covers, with the overlap consequence restricted to positive minimum cap mass.
pk-intake-independent-normal-strict-cap-.statement:
Let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a convex body of volume $V$, and let $H_1,\ldots,H_j$ be proper closed halfspaces covering $K$, where $2\le j\le D$. Assume their normals are linearly independent. With $A_i=|K\cap H_i|$ and $\gamma_q=(q/(q+1))^q$ for $q\ge1$, for every $\alpha>0$,
$$
\sum_{i=1}^j(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_{j-1}}>V.
$$
If $a=\min_i A_i>0$, then $\sum_i A_i-V>(j-1/\gamma_{j-1})a$.

pk-intake-integer-mean-closed-tail.relation_to_goal: The scalar result assumes an exactly integral mean. The mixed-geometric consequence concerns vertical caps with one integer coordinate and integer continuous dimension.
pk-intake-integer-mean-closed-tail.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be real and let $(a_i)_{i=\ell}^r$ be positive probability masses on consecutive integers with concave $d$th roots. Suppose $\mu=\sum_{i=\ell}^r i a_i$ is an integer. Both closed tails satisfy
$$
\sum_{i\ge\mu}a_i>\left(\frac{d+1}{d+2}\right)^{d+1},
\qquad
\sum_{i\le\mu}a_i>\left(\frac{d+1}{d+2}\right)^{d+1}.
$$
At every fixed $d$ this constant is the infimum of either tail among profiles with exactly integer mean.

For the geometric consequence, let $d$ be a positive integer and $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ a convex body with positive mixed $d$-volume $W$. If the base coordinate of its mixed-volume centroid is an integer, every closed vertical halfspace containing the centroid has mixed $d$-volume strictly greater than $W((d+1)/(d+2))^{d+1}$. This normalized bound is also sharp as an infimum.

pk-intake-interval-path.relation_to_goal: A finite Hausdorff-continuous deformation for three positive interval fibers at n=d=1, with a retained zero-length endpoint and exact terminal depth.
pk-intake-interval-path.statement:
Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R$ be a convex body whose only nonempty integer fibers are positive-length intervals at three consecutive bases. Choose the shorter of the two endpoint intervals, choosing either if their lengths agree. For a body $K$ of positive total integer fiber length $W(K)$, let $h_K(p)$ be the infimum of the total integer fiber length in a closed ambient halfspace containing the mixed point $p$. Write $D(K)=\max_{p\in K\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R)}h_K(p)/W(K)$.

There is a path of convex bodies from $C$, continuous in the Hausdorff metric, on which $D$ is continuous and nonincreasing. The same three integer bases remain nonempty throughout. The chosen endpoint interval has nonincreasing length, is never globally deepest while its length is positive, and ends as a retained singleton of zero length. The other endpoint keeps its initial positive length, and the middle interval ends with that same length, so the two positive fibers are adjacent and $D$ at the terminal body is $1/4$. One-dimensional length is used throughout. There are at most four nonconstant pieces: an optional Minkowski segment (affine in support functions) followed by convex hulls of the three lifted intervals with endpoints affine in the parameter of each piece.

pk-intake-inverse-power-density-centerpo.relation_to_goal: Continuous Lebesgue densities with a specified convex inverse power. The statement concerns the maximum depth in one continuous space.
pk-intake-inverse-power-density-centerpo.statement: Let $r\ge1$ be an integer. Let $f$ be a bounded nonnegative upper-semicontinuous density of compact support in $\mathbb R^r$. Assume $\{f>0\}$ has nonempty interior and the function $f^{-1/(r+1)}$, extended by $+\infty$ where $f=0$, is convex. Then there is a point $y$ in the interior of the support of $f$ such that every closed halfspace containing $y$ has $f$-mass at least $\gamma_r\int f$, where $\gamma_r=(r/(r+1))^r$. The constant is sharp.

pk-intake-joint-projective-energy-marked.relation_to_goal: Ordinary marked convex bodies and actual compact convex fibers with full-dimensional interior marks. The result is an energy interpolation statement without a mixed halfspace-depth estimate.
pk-intake-joint-projective-energy-marked.statement:
Let $d,m\ge1$, let $K_i\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies, and choose $y_i\in\operatorname{int}K_i$ and weights $\lambda_i\ge0$ with $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. Use the energy $E_K(y)=\min_{a:\,1+a\cdot(x-y)>0\ (x\in K)}\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$. Put $M=\sum_i\lambda_i K_i$ and $y=\sum_i\lambda_i y_i$. Then $y\in\operatorname{int}M$ and
$$
E_M(y)^{1/d}\ \ge\ \sum_i\lambda_i E_{K_i}(y_i)^{1/d}.
$$
Equality holds exactly when the centered bodies $K_i-y_i$ with $\lambda_i>0$ are positive scalar multiples of one another. In particular $y\mapsto E_K(y)^{1/d}$ is strictly concave on $\operatorname{int}K$.

If $H$ is a convex body containing $M$, the same lower bound holds for $E_H(y)^{1/d}$. Equality then requires both $H=M$ and the same marked homothety condition. Consequently, for a compact convex set $C\subset\mathbb R^{n+d}$ with fibers $C_z=\{x:(z,x)\in C\}$, the function $(z,y)\mapsto E_{C_z}(y)^{1/d}$ is jointly concave on the convex domain $\{(z,y): y\in\operatorname{int}_{\mathbb R^d}C_z\}$.

pk-intake-larger-hull-selector-obstructi.relation_to_goal: PK's fixed three-fiber example rules out the prescribed middle hull at the sharp threshold. This cap certificate does not bound points outside that hull and makes no claim against the locked weak conjecture.
pk-intake-larger-hull-selector-obstructi.statement:
Let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^5:x_i\ge0,\ \sum_i x_i\le1\}$, $V=|B|=1/120$, and $g=(1/6,\ldots,1/6)$. Set $R=9/2$, $r=497/3000$, $\ell=11/12-Rr$, and $T=1-r-\ell=3979/6000$. Let $D$ be the simplex with vertices $p=(0,11/12,0,0,0)$, $b_0=(r,\ell,0,0,0)$, and $b_0+T e_i$ for $i=2,3,4,5$. Put

$$
m=|D|/V=rT^4=\frac{124581095445185057}{3888000000000000000},
\qquad q=m^{-1/5},\qquad A=(2-q)D,\qquad C=qD,
\qquad a=(2m^{1/5}-1)^5.
$$

The convex body $L=\operatorname{conv}((\{-1\}\times A)\cup(\{0\}\times B)\cup(\{1\}\times C))$ has exactly the three integer fibers $A,B,C$ at $-1,0,1$, with volumes $aV,V,V$ and $0<a<10^{-5}$. Each fiber has strictly less than half the total mixed volume. Write $\mu(H)$ for the summed five-dimensional volumes of the integer fibers of $L$ in an ambient halfspace $H$, and $\Gamma_5=(5/6)^5$.

Set $h_1=1/6-(2/25)a$ and $h_2=1/6+(17/50)a$. The two proper closed ambient halfspaces

$$
H_1=\{(z,x):x_1+(1-q)rz\ge h_1\},\qquad
H_2=\{(z,x):x_2-2z\ge h_2\}
$$

cover $\{0\}\times\operatorname{conv}(\{g\}\cup D)$. Their respective mixed masses in units of $V$ are

$$
\frac{\mu(H_1)}{V}=\Gamma_5[1+(12/125)a]^5,\qquad
\frac{\mu(H_2)}{V}=\Gamma_5[1-(51/125)a]^5+a.
$$

Both are strictly below $\Gamma_5(1+a/2)$. Consequently the maximum original mixed depth normalized by $(2+a)V$ on $\{0\}\times\operatorname{conv}(\{g\}\cup D)$ is strictly below $\Gamma_5/2$.

pk-intake-midpoint-label-balanced-face-a.relation_to_goal: Finite atomic face-incidence rigidity for positive weights with actual same-label midpoint membership.
pk-intake-midpoint-label-balanced-face-a.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite subset of a real affine space, with $k$ occupied labels. Assume the geometric midpoint of every pair of distinct points of the same label belongs to $P$. Give each $p\in P$ a weight $w_p>0$, put $M=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$, $Q=\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and $\alpha=M/k$, and set $w(F)=\sum_{p\in P\cap F}w_p$ for each face $F$ of $Q$, allowing $Q$ itself. Let $\mathcal F$ be the faces of weight $\alpha$, and write $\chi_F$ for their incidence vectors on $P$.

Exactly one of the following holds.

1. There is $v\in\mathbb R^P$ with $\sum_{p\in P}v_p=0$ and $v\cdot\chi_F<0$ for every $F\in\mathcal F$. When $\mathcal F$ is empty, $v=0$ works.
2. The set $P$ consists of exactly $k$ vertices of $Q$, all of weight $\alpha$.

Moreover, a nonnegative combination $\sum_{F\in\mathcal F}\lambda_F\chi_F=\mathbf 1_P$ exists precisely in case 2. In that case its coefficients are $\lambda_{\{p\}}=1$ for all $p\in P$.

pk-intake-midpoint-label-strict-minimal-.relation_to_goal: A finite weighted centerpoint with a strict original minimal-face mass alternative for midpoint-closed labels.
pk-intake-midpoint-label-strict-minimal-.statement:
Let $P$ be a nonempty finite set in a real affine space with $k$ occupied labels. For every pair of distinct points of the same label, assume their geometric midpoint belongs to $P$. Give the points positive weights $w_p$, with total $M=\sum_{p\in P}w_p$. Let $Q=\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and let $F_p$ be the unique face of $Q$ whose relative interior contains $p$, allowing $Q$ itself. Write $w(F)=\sum_{p\in P\cap F}w_p$ and let $\delta_w(p)$ be the minimum weight in any closed affine halfspace containing $p$. The whole-space trace is allowed and is the sole trace containing $p$ in rank zero.

There exists $p\in P$ with $\delta_w(p)\ge M/k$. Such a point can be chosen with $w(F_p)>M/k$ except exactly when $P$ consists of $k$ vertices of $Q$ of weight $M/k$ each. In the exception every point has $\delta_w(p)=w(F_p)=M/k$. In particular, strict minimal-face mass holds for some center whenever $|P|>k$.

For a finite nonempty complete subset $P=Q\cap(c+L)$ of an affine lattice, the labels can be the occupied cosets modulo $2L$. Then $k\le 2^{\operatorname{rank} L}$, including rank zero. For a finite graph $P=\{(p,g_p):p\in P_0\}$ over an affine-lattice base, the labels can be the occupied base parities if every distinct same-parity pair $p,q\in P_0$ has $m=(p+q)/2\in P_0$ and $g_m=(g_p+g_q)/2$. In this graph case the depth and the minimal face are taken in the lifted space.

pk-intake-nested-three-fiber-depth.relation_to_goal: The common-core center and the $\gamma_d/2$ lower bound for inclusion-ordered compatible triples, with $n=1$ and arbitrary $d\ge1$.
pk-intake-nested-three-fiber-depth.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and let $A,B,C\subset\mathbb R^d$ be convex bodies with $(A+C)/2\subseteq B$. Set $S=(\{-1\}\times A)\cup(\{0\}\times B)\cup(\{1\}\times C)$, measured by summing $d$-dimensional volumes on its three fibers. If a convex body $K$ satisfies $A\subseteq K\subseteq B\cap C$, let $a=|A|$, $V=|K|$, $E=|B|+|C|-2V$ and let $g_K$ be the volume centroid of $K$. Then the actual point $(0,g_K)$ has normalized mixed halfspace depth at least
$$
\frac{\gamma_d V+a/2}{2V+E+a}.
$$
This is at least $\gamma_d/2$ if $E\le(1/\gamma_d-1)a$. In particular, for $B=C=K$ the displayed bound holds with $E=0$, and the same conclusion holds at the actual middle centroid when $B$ and $C$ are translates of one another, taking $V=|B|$.

If $A,B,C$ are totally ordered by inclusion, some actual mixed point has normalized depth at least $\gamma_d/2$. The same holds if such an order is obtained by an affine change preserving $\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d$, including a shear affine in the integer base.

pk-intake-open-cover-strict-cap-profile.relation_to_goal: Gives strictness for a fixed ordinary density cover when every point of positive support is in the interior of some cap.
pk-intake-open-cover-strict-cap-profile.statement:
Let $r\ge1$ and $\beta\ge r+1$. Let $f$ be a Lebesgue density of mass $M\in(0,\infty)$, positive on a nonempty open convex set $U\subset\mathbb R^r$ and zero outside $U$. Assume $f^{-1/\beta}$ is finite, positive and convex on $U$. Let finitely many proper closed halfspaces $H_i$ satisfy $U\subset\bigcup_i\operatorname{int}H_i$, and write $A_i=\int_{H_i}f$ and $\gamma_r=(r/(r+1))^r$. For every $\alpha>0$,
$$
\sum_i(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_r}>M,
\qquad x_+=\max\{x,0\}.
$$

pk-intake-ordinary-cap-profile-equality.relation_to_goal: Classifies equality for ordinary volume with exactly D+1 halfspaces. The projected density and mixed-integer problems have additional hypotheses.
pk-intake-ordinary-cap-profile-equality.statement:
Let $D\ge2$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^D$ be a convex body of volume $V$, and let $D+1$ closed halfspaces $H_i$ with nonzero normals cover $K$. Write $A_i=|K\cap H_i|$, $\gamma_D=(D/(D+1))^D$ and $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. For $\alpha>0$,
$$
\sum_i(A_i-\alpha)_+ + \frac{\alpha}{\gamma_D}=V
$$
if and only if $K$ is a simplex, the $H_i$ are its $D+1$ distinct vertex halfspaces through its centroid and parallel to the opposite facets, and $\alpha=A_i=\gamma_D V$ for every $i$.

pk-intake-ordinary-depth-descent-by-supp.relation_to_goal: A local upper-cover argument for ordinary uniform maximal depth under an actual full critical circuit. It yields a derivative of the cover bound and uses equality at the starting body. It supplies no bound for the locked mixed-integer problem.
pk-intake-ordinary-depth-descent-by-supp.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$. Suppose the $d+1$ unit vectors $u_i$ span $\mathbb R^d$ and form a minimal positive circuit, and that $\theta_i>0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$ satisfy $\sum_i\theta_i S_i u_i=0$, where $S_i=\mathcal H^{d-1}(K\cap u_i^\perp)$. As in the stationary setting, suppose the sections have centroid $0$. Assume the central cap masses $|K\cap\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}|$ all equal $Q$, where $Q$ is the maximum over $y\in K$ of $\inf_{H\ni y}|K\cap H|$ for closed halfspaces $H$. Then the selected caps attain the depth at the deepest point $0$.

Take a bump $K_t$ as in the section-preserving support-bump lemma with signature weight $W\ne Q/|K|$. Such a bump exists if $h$ is $C^2$ with everywhere positive-definite $A_h$. For small signed $t$ there are a point $y(t)$ near $0$ and $d+1$ parallel translates of the respective original caps through $y(t)$, all with the same mass $q(t)$. They cover $\mathbb R^d$ and bound the new maximum raw depth by $q(t)$. The normalized cover bound has derivative
$$
\left.\frac{d}{dt}\frac{q(t)}{|K_t|}\right|_{t=0}
=\left(W-\frac Q{|K|}\right)\frac{V'_0}{|K|}.
$$
For all sufficiently small nonzero $t$ of the appropriate sign, the maximal normalized ordinary depth of $K_t$ is strictly below that of $K$.

pk-intake-paired-centroid-tails.relation_to_goal: A one-dimensional marginal inequality and its symmetric convolution and Cartesian product consequences.
pk-intake-paired-centroid-tails.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$, and let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body with volume centroid $g$. For uniform $X$ on $K$, $u\ne0$, and $F(s)=\mathbb P(u\cdot(X-g)\ge s)$,
$$
F(s)+F(-s)\ge2\gamma_d\qquad(s\ge0).
$$
For $d\ge2$ the same bound holds with $F(s)=\mathbb P(Z\ge s)$ for any compactly supported, nonatomic, centered $1/d$-concave probability law of $Z$ on the line. In particular, for any independent random vector $Y\in\mathbb R^d$ with a distribution symmetric about zero, every closed halfspace through $g$ has $\mathbb P(X+Y\in H)\ge\gamma_d$. If $Y$ has finite first moment, the convolution has centroid $g$.

For a product of convex bodies $P\times K$ with $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ centrally symmetric about $j\in\mathbb Z^n$, every closed ambient halfspace containing $(j,g)$ has normalized mixed-integer mass at least $\gamma_d$.

pk-intake-paired-maximum-depth-simplex-r.relation_to_goal: Ordinary convex bodies in integer dimensions d≥3. The stability conclusion gives a qualitative gap on each specified compact class.
pk-intake-paired-maximum-depth-simplex-r.statement:
Let $d\ge3$ be an integer, $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ a convex body, $\mu_K$ its normalized volume, and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. Define
$$
p_K(y)=\inf_{\substack{u\ne0\\s\in\mathbb R}}\frac{\mu_K\{x:u\cdot(x-y)\ge s\}+\mu_K\{x:u\cdot(x-y)\ge -s\}}{2}.
$$
The maximum $D_{\rm pair}(K)=\max_{y\in K}p_K(y)$ exists, satisfies $D_{\rm pair}(K)\ge\Gamma_d$, and equals $\Gamma_d$ exactly for simplices.

For fixed $0<r\le R$ and $\varepsilon>0$, consider the bodies with $rB_2^d\subseteq K\subseteq RB_2^d$ whose Hausdorff distance to the set of full-dimensional simplices is at least $\varepsilon$. If this class is nonempty, then $D_{\rm pair}(K)-\Gamma_d$ attains a strictly positive minimum on it.

pk-intake-positive-projective-chart-glob.relation_to_goal: One source chart with freely chosen base coefficient on a finite anchored hull. The cut conclusion uses a lattice-complete finite base and concerns the actual nested bodies and local inward speeds.
pk-intake-positive-projective-chart-glob.statement:
Let $d\ge1$. Let $P\subset\mathbb R^n$ be finite and nonempty, let each $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ for $z\in P$ be a convex body, and assume the sampled anchored Minkowski inclusions. Put $C=\operatorname{conv}\bigcup_{z\in P}(\{z\}\times K_z)$. Fix $p\in P$ and $y\in\operatorname{int}K_p$, and let $a_y$ be the optimal parameter for $E_{K_p}(y)=\min_a\int_{K_p}[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over positive denominators. There exists a fixed base vector $b$ for which
$$
L(z,x)=1+a_y\cdot(x-y)+b\cdot(z-p),\qquad
\min_C L=\min_{x\in K_p}[1+a_y\cdot(x-y)]\ge\frac1{d+1}.
$$
For every threshold $0<\delta<1/(d+1)$, a tangent continuation of $t^{-d}$ below $\delta$ is inactive on a neighborhood of $C$ when evaluated at $L$.

If $P=\operatorname{conv}(P)\cap\mathbb Z^n$, choose any continuous anchored support majorant $\ell(u,z)=h_{K_p}(u)+A_p(u)\cdot(z-p)\ge h_{K_z}(u)$ on $P$ for each unit $u$. Then the pure inverse-power cuts
$$
C_\varepsilon=C\cap\bigcap_{u\in\mathbb S^{d-1}}
\{(z,x):u\cdot x+\varepsilon h_{K_p-y}(u)L(z,x)^{-d}\le \ell(u,z)\}
$$
give a nested compact convex deformation for all sufficiently small $\varepsilon\ge0$, in $\operatorname{aff}(P)\times\mathbb R^d$, with projection $\operatorname{conv}(P)$ and positive integer fibers exactly at $P$. On the source fiber the cuts are exactly the prescribed single-source cuts with denominator $1+a_y\cdot(x-y)$. At a regular old boundary point $x\in\partial K_z$ with normal $\nu$, the inward first speed is $h_{K_p-y}(\nu)L(z,x)^{-d}$ if $\ell(\nu,z)=h_{K_z}(\nu)$, and zero otherwise.

pk-intake-positive-right-index-knot-defi.relation_to_goal: Pointwise scalar diagonal-envelope estimate on admissible positive-right-index knots. Global maximization and geometric halfspace-depth applications are separate.
pk-intake-positive-right-index-knot-defi.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and $H,J$ be integers with $1\le J\le H\le(2d+1)J+d$. Put $t=1/(d+1)$ and $\Gamma=(dt)^d$. Define the double knot
$$
a=\frac{t(H+J+1)}{H(2J+1)},\qquad
\beta=\frac{t(H-J)}{dH(2J+1)}.
$$
Write $x_+=\max\{x,0\}$. For $h\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ put $r_h=(1-ah)_+$, $q_h=t-\beta h$, and $p_h=t+\beta(h+1)$. Define the finite diagonal-envelope deficit by
$$
D=\Gamma\sum_{h\ge0}r_h^d
-d^d\sum_{\substack{h\ge0\\r_h>0}}\left[q_h^{d-1}(r_h-dq_h)_++p_h^{d-1}(r_h-dp_h)_+\right].
$$
The thresholds in the second sum are positive, and $D/\Gamma\le-1/1080$.

pk-intake-projective-energy-attainment-e.relation_to_goal: Ordinary full-dimensional compact convex bodies at interior marks. The escort is an ordinary Lebesgue density and the projective volume is computed in the continuous coordinates.
pk-intake-projective-energy-attainment-e.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with nonempty interior, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$ put $L_a(x)=1+a\cdot(x-y)$ and define
$$
E_K(y)=\inf_{\{a:L_a>0\ \text{on }K\}}\int_K L_a(x)^{-d-1}\,dx.
$$
The infimum is positive and attained at a unique admissible $a_*$, and $E_K(y)$ is the minimum $d$-volume of the images of $K-y$ under $w\mapsto w/(1+a\cdot w)$ over these $a$. For $L=L_{a_*}$ and $E=E_K(y)$,
$$
\int_K (x-y)L(x)^{-d-2}\,dx=0,\qquad
\int_K L(x)^{-d-2}\,dx=\int_K L(x)^{-d-1}\,dx=E.
$$
Thus $\rho=L^{-d-2}/E$ on $K$ is a probability density with barycenter $y$ and $\int_K L\rho\,dx=1$. Its restriction to $K$ extends to a smooth positive function on a neighborhood of $K$.

For every invertible linear $Q$ and every $b\in\mathbb R^d$, $E_{QK+b}(Qy+b)=|\det Q|E_K(y)$. If $K\subset H$ for another convex body $H$, then $E_K(y)\le E_H(y)$ with equality exactly when $K=H$. Writing $g_K=|K|^{-1}\int_K x\,dx$ for the ordinary centroid, $E_K(y)\le |K|$ with equality exactly when $y=g_K$.

pk-intake-projective-energy-envelope-den.relation_to_goal: A single full-dimensional ordinary body and a fiber-interior mark. The floor holds for the optimizing affine denominator.
pk-intake-projective-energy-envelope-den.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Define $E_K(y)=\min_a\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over $a$ for which the denominator is positive on $K$, and let $a_y$ be its unique minimizer. The maps $y\mapsto a_y$ and $y\mapsto E_K(y)$ are smooth on $\operatorname{int}K$ and
$$
\nabla_y E_K(y)=(d+1)E_K(y)a_y,\qquad
\nabla_y E_K(y)^{1/d}=\frac{d+1}{d}E_K(y)^{1/d}a_y.
$$
The optimal denominator $1+a_y\cdot(x-y)$ is at least $1/(d+1)$ on $K$ and strictly greater than $1/(d+1)$ on $\operatorname{int}K$.

pk-intake-projective-energy-ordinary-ent.relation_to_goal: Ordinary Lebesgue densities on a convex body with a fixed interior barycenter. The feasible class has no pointwise density cap.
pk-intake-projective-energy-ordinary-ent.statement:
Let $d\ge1$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a convex body, and let $y\in\operatorname{int}K$. Put $p=(d+1)/(d+2)$ and let $E_K(y)$ be the minimum of $\int_K[1+a\cdot(x-y)]^{-d-1}\,dx$ over affine denominators strictly positive on $K$. Then
$$
E_K(y)=\max_{\substack{\rho\ge0,\ \int_K\rho\,dx=1\\\int_K x\rho(x)\,dx=y}}
\left(\int_K\rho(x)^p\,dx\right)^{d+2}.
$$
The maximum is over ordinary Lebesgue densities on $K$ with the displayed mass and mean. Its unique maximizer up to Lebesgue null sets is $\rho=L^{-d-2}/E_K(y)$, where $L(x)=1+a_*\cdot(x-y)$ is the attained optimal denominator.

pk-intake-quartic-continuous-kernel-gain.relation_to_goal: Scalar continuous kernels for affine simplex-chain envelopes. Discrete sampling and the mixed halfspace-depth conclusion require separate arguments.
pk-intake-quartic-continuous-kernel-gain.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ be an integer, $\theta=d/(d+1)$, and $f(z)=(1+z)^{d+1}/(1+\theta z)^d$ for $z\ge-1$. For every $v\in[0,1]$,
$$
f(v)+f(-v)\ge 2+\theta v^2+\frac{\theta}{4}v^4,
$$
with equality exactly at $v=0$.

For $z\in[-1,1]$, let $K_z(x)=(1+zx)^{d-1}[1-(d+1+dz)x]$ for $0\le x\le 1/(d+1+dz)$ and let $K_z(x)=0$ for larger $x$. Put $A_d(v)=\int_0^\infty (K_v(x)+K_{-v}(x))\,dx$. Then $A_d(v)=[f(v)+f(-v)-2]/(dv^2)$ for $v>0$, and $A_d(0)=1/(d+1)$ is its continuous extension. In particular,
$$
A_d(v)\ge\frac{1+v^2/4}{d+1}\qquad(0\le v\le 1),
$$
with equality exactly at $v=0$.

pk-intake-real-degree-centered-slab-tail.relation_to_goal: A real-degree scalar tail estimate and its application to outer vertical regions with one integer coordinate.
pk-intake-real-degree-centered-slab-tail.statement:
Let $d\ge1$ be real, and let $(w_i)$ be a nonzero nonnegative sequence on a finite consecutive integer interval, with $(w_i^{1/d})$ concave there and $\sum_i i w_i=0$. Put $M=\sum_i w_i$, $m=\max_i w_i$, $r_d=(2/(d+2))^{(d+1)/d}$ and $\kappa_d=1/(3+d r_d)$. For every integer $h\ge0$,
$$
\min\left\{\sum_{i>h}w_i,\ \sum_{i<-h}w_i\right\}
\ge\kappa_d\bigl[M-(2h+1)m\bigr].
$$
The constants satisfy $1/5<\kappa_d\le9/31<3/10$, with $\kappa_1=9/31$ and $\lim_{d\to\infty}\kappa_d=1/5$.

Let $d$ be a positive integer and $C\subseteq\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ a convex body of positive mixed $d$-volume $M$ whose mixed-volume centroid has integer base coordinate $j$. Write $w_i=\operatorname{vol}_d(C_i)$ and $m=\max_{i\in\mathbb Z} w_i$. With $\kappa_d$ as above, each of $z>j+h$ and $z<j-h$ has mixed $d$-volume in $C\cap(\mathbb Z\times\mathbb R^d)$ at least $\kappa_d[M-(2h+1)m]$ for every integer $h\ge0$.

pk-intake-section-preserving-support-bum.relation_to_goal: A deformation and weighted-cap statement for ordinary uniform volume. The feasibility argument is local in normal space and gives no admissible deformation for a general singular patch or a compatible mixed-fiber family.
pk-intake-section-preserving-support-bum.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body with $0\in\operatorname{int}K$, and let $u_1,\ldots,u_m$ be unit vectors. Write $H_i=\{x:u_i\cdot x\ge0\}$, $V=|K|$, and $\Phi(K)=\sum_i\theta_i|K\cap H_i|/V$ for weights $\theta_i>0$ with $\sum_i\theta_i=1$. Let $h$ be the support function of $K$ on the unit sphere. Take a nonzero $C^2$ function $\psi\ge0$ on the sphere such that on an open neighborhood of $\operatorname{supp}\psi$, $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h=\nabla_S^2 h+hI$ is positive definite on each spherical tangent space. Suppose the support points $X(n)=h(n)n+\nabla_S h(n)$ for $n\in\operatorname{supp}\psi$ satisfy $s_i u_i\cdot X(n)>0$ for fixed signs $s_i\in\{-1,1\}$ and every $i$.

For all sufficiently small signed $t$, $h_t=h+t\psi$ is the support function of a convex body $K_t$ with $0\in\operatorname{int}K_t$. The changed radial intervals are in $\{x:s_i u_i\cdot x>0\text{ for all }i\}$ and stay uniformly away from the cutting planes. In particular $K_t\cap u_i^\perp=K\cap u_i^\perp$ for all $i$. Set $V_t=|K_t|$, $\Delta V(t)=V_t-V$, $e_i=\mathbf1_{\{s_i=1\}}$, and $W=\sum_i\theta_i e_i$. Then
$$
|K_t\cap H_i|-|K\cap H_i|=e_i\Delta V(t),\qquad
\Phi(K_t)-\Phi(K)=(W-\Phi(K))\,\frac{\Delta V(t)}{V_t}.
$$
The volume $V_t$ is $C^1$ near $0$, $\Delta V(t)$ has the sign of $t$ for $t\ne0$, and
$$
V'_0=\int_{\partial K}\psi(n(x))\,d\mathcal H^{d-1}(x)>0
$$
where $n(x)$ is the outward unit normal wherever it is unique.

At a Hausdorff local minimum of $\Phi$ subject to the same section traces, every such patch has $W=\Phi(K)$. Group the $u_i$ by their unoriented planes. A positive-curvature patch crossing exactly one such plane at a point on no other distinct plane excludes a local minimum if the two orientations in that class have unequal total weights. If $h$ is $C^2$ and $A_h>0$ on the entire sphere, an imbalanced class always gives such a patch. If all classes balance, $\Phi(K)=1/2$ for every $K$.

pk-intake-sharp-integer-centroid-partiti.relation_to_goal: Bounds the number of positive convex cells, not the number of source fibers within a cell. It gives no lower bound on mixed centroid depth or assertion of a recursive single-cut partition.
pk-intake-sharp-integer-centroid-partiti.statement:
Let $n,d$ be positive integers and let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body. Write $\Lambda=\mathbb Z^n\times\mathbb R^d$, $S=C\cap\Lambda$, and assume $q=\dim_{\mathrm H}S\ge1$. Then $C$ is the union of $k\le2^n$ closed affine-score winner cells that are ambient convex bodies, each cut from $C$ by at most $k-1$ closed halfspaces. Every mixed piece $D_i\cap\Lambda$ has dimension $q$ and positive $\mathcal H_q$ measure. Distinct mixed pieces overlap in $\mathcal H_q$-null sets. The actual centroid of $\mathcal H_q|_{D_i\cap\Lambda}$ belongs to $D_i\cap\Lambda$, and the distinct centroid bases are exactly the vertices and all the lattice points of their convex hull. In particular $\sum_i\mathcal H_q(D_i\cap\Lambda)=\mathcal H_q(S)$.

The universal count $2^n$ is sharp already for $q=d$, even if fractional splitting of the mixed measure is allowed instead of convex cells.

pk-intake-sharp-scalar-trimming.relation_to_goal: A scalar estimate for the volume of the retained endpoint copy.
pk-intake-sharp-scalar-trimming.statement:
For every integer $d\ge2$, every $s\ge r>0$, and every $0\le\varepsilon\le r/2$,
$$
(r-2\varepsilon)^d\ge\frac{r^d+s^d-(s+\varepsilon)^d}{2}.
$$
The uniform coefficient $1/2$ is optimal, with equality and a positive bracket at $d=2$, $s=r$, $\varepsilon=r/3$.

pk-intake-sharp-simplex-vertex-averaging.relation_to_goal: Continuous test functions on an ordinary simplex. The statement concerns the simplex probability laws, without a mixed-integer center assertion.
pk-intake-sharp-simplex-vertex-averaging.statement:
Let $d\ge2$, let $Z$ be uniform on the simplex $\Delta_d=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$, and let $I$ be independent and uniform on its vertex indices. For $0\le b\le1$ set $Y_b=(1-b)Z+be_I$. Then $Y_b\preceq_{\mathrm{cx}} Z$ if and only if $b\le1/d$, where the order means $\mathbb E\phi(Y_b)\le\mathbb E\phi(Z)$ for every continuous convex $\phi$ on $\Delta_d$. Equivalently the inequality reverses for every continuous concave test.

At $b=1/d$, there is a coupling $(Y,X)$ of $Y_{1/d}$ and $Z$ with $\mathbb E[X\mid Y]=Y$ in which the minimum coordinate value and its unique index agree almost surely. The common minimum has survival function $(1-ds)_+^{d-1}$ for $s\ge0$. In fact for every $b\ge1/d$, $\mathbb E\min_j(Y_b)_j=(1-b)/(d(d-1))$, whereas $\mathbb E\min_j Z_j=1/d^2$.

At $b=0$ every test gives equality. For $0<b<1/d$ equality holds precisely for affine tests. At $b=1/d$ equality holds precisely when the test is affine on every slice $\{x\in\Delta_d:x_i=t/d,\ x_j\ge t/d\text{ for all }j\ne i\}$, for every $i$ and $0\le t\le1$. In particular the minimum is a nonaffine concave equality test at the critical step. When $d=2$ and $b=1/2$ the whole laws agree. For $d\ge3$ the critical comparison is strict for every strictly convex test.

pk-intake-simplex-beta-step-merging.relation_to_goal: Ordinary uniform simplex transport. The conditional mean is for the stated independent-step construction.
pk-intake-simplex-beta-step-merging.statement: For an integer $m\ge1$, let $\mu_m$ be uniform probability on $\Delta_m=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$. Independently draw $W\sim\mu_m$, a uniform index $J\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and $R$ with density $m(1-r)^{m-1}$ on $(0,1)$. Write $e_j$ for the standard basis vectors. Then $X=(1-R)W+Re_J$ has law $\mu_m$. Given $J=j$, its law has density $mx_j$ relative to $\mu_m$. For $V=(mW+e_J)/(m+1)$, one has $\mathbb E[X\mid W,J]=V$ and hence $\mathbb E[X\mid V,J]=\mathbb E[X\mid V]=V$.

pk-intake-simplex-independent-step-densi.relation_to_goal: Ordinary simplex stationarity for independent absolutely continuous step laws in at least three coordinates. The atom examples record stationary laws outside the uniqueness class.
pk-intake-simplex-independent-step-densi.statement: For an integer $m\ge3$, let $W$ be uniform on the simplex $\Delta_m=\{x\in\mathbb R^m:x_j\ge0,\ \sum_jx_j=1\}$, let $J$ be uniform on its vertex indices, and let $B$ have an absolutely continuous probability density $w$ on $[0,1]$. Assume the three variables are independent. Then $(1-B)W+Be_J$ is uniform on $\Delta_m$ if and only if $w(b)=m(1-b)^{m-1}$ almost everywhere. If an atom at zero is allowed, any mixture of this beta law and the unit mass at zero is stationary. For $m=2$ the constant step $B=1/2$ is also stationary.

pk-intake-single-parity-depth-retention.relation_to_goal: Compares two sampling rules and two admissible sets for the same full-dimensional body, allowing a codimension-one fine hull. The fine depth is at least $\gamma_s/2^m$, since $2m\le2^m$, and hence exceeds even the sharp ambient fine target $\gamma_s/2^{m+1}$. The locked conjecture concerns one sampling law and a lower bound in terms of its own mass.
pk-intake-single-parity-depth-retention.statement:
Let $m,s\ge1$ be integers, let $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and let $K\subset\mathbb R^s$ be a full-dimensional simplex of volume $V$ and centroid $c$. Put $\gamma_s=(s/(s+1))^s$, $Q_m=\{p\in\mathbb R^m:\sum_i |p_i|\le1\}$, $g(p)=(1+\sum_i p_i)/2$, and
$$
C=\{(p,u,x)\in\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^s:
p\in Q_m,\ |u-g(p)|\le\varepsilon,\ x\in K\}.
$$
The body $C$ is full-dimensional. The coarse rule requires $p\in\mathbb Z^m$, with admissible set $S_{\mathrm c}=C\cap(\mathbb Z^m\times\mathbb R^{1+s})$ and measure $\mathcal H_{s+1}|_{S_{\mathrm c}}$. The fine rule additionally requires $u\in\mathbb Z$, with admissible set $S_{\mathrm f}=C\cap(\mathbb Z^{m+1}\times\mathbb R^s)$ and measure $\mathcal H_s|_{S_{\mathrm f}}$. For each rule normalize its measure by its own total mass. Define its maximum depth as the maximum over its admissible set of the infimum of normalized mass of all closed ambient halfspaces containing the point.

The coarse rule has $2m+1$ fibers of mass $2\varepsilon V$ and maximum depth $D_{\mathrm c}=\gamma_s$, attained at $(0,1/2,c)$. The fine rule has exactly $2m$ fibers of mass $V$, at $(e_i,1)$ and $(-e_i,0)$ for $1\le i\le m$, and maximum depth $D_{\mathrm f}=\gamma_s/(2m)$, attained at the centroid of each fiber. The ambient normalized laws are mutually singular. After projection to $(p,x)$, their total variation distance, defined by the supremum over measurable sets, is exactly $1/(2m+1)$, the coarse probability of the omitted base $p=0$.

The affine span of the fine bases has dimension $m$. Its integer points project bijectively to the odd-sum coset of the index-two even-sum sublattice of $\mathbb Z^m$. The fine mixed hull is $\operatorname{conv}(S_{\mathrm f})=\{(p,g(p),x):p\in Q_m,\ x\in K\}$ and has codimension one in $C$. Replacing $C$ by this hull preserves the fine set and fine measure and reduces the original coarse $\mathcal H_{s+1}$ mass to zero.

Thus for fixed $s$ and $\varepsilon$, a single added integer condition of projected index two gives $D_{\mathrm f}/D_{\mathrm c}=1/(2m)\to0$ with projected total variation tending to zero. In particular there is no positive dimension-independent retention factor for this comparison, even when the omitted coarse base marginal mass is arbitrarily small.

pk-intake-strict-nonzero-shift-centroid-.relation_to_goal: Scalar probability theorem and its ordinary convex-body specialization in integer dimensions d≥3. The strict bound concerns each fixed nonzero shift at the volume centroid.
pk-intake-strict-nonzero-shift-centroid-.statement:
Let $d\ge3$ be an integer and $\Gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$. If $Z$ has a compactly supported, nonatomic, centered $1/d$-concave probability law on $\mathbb R$, then for every $s\ne0$,
$$
\mathbb P(Z\ge s)+\mathbb P(Z\ge -s)>2\Gamma_d.
$$
In particular, if $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ is a convex body with volume $V>0$ and centroid $g$, then for each $u\ne0$ and $s\ne0$ the two closed caps $K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge s\}$ and $K\cap\{x:u\cdot(x-g)\ge -s\}$ have total volume greater than $2\Gamma_d V$.

pk-intake-target-mass-source-fiber-obstr.relation_to_goal: A counterexample to the bound of $2^n$ on the number of source fibers used by a dominated fixed-mass selection with prescribed centroid.
pk-intake-target-mass-source-fiber-obstr.statement:

Set $P=\{-2,-1,0,1,2\}^n$, $C=[-2,2]^n	imes K$, and let $\mu$ be the original mixed measure on $S=P	imes K$, namely $\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathbf 1_K\,dx)$. Its mass is $W=5^n a$. Every $0\le
u\le\mu$ of mass $m=2^{-n}W$ has at least $\lceil(5/2)^nceil>2^n$ bases $z$ with $
u(\{z\}	imes K)>0$.

Among these measures with full centroid zero, $\int\|z\|_2^2\,d
u(z,x)$ attains its minimum. Let $r$ be the smallest squared radius occurring on $P$ such that $a\,\#\{z\in P:\|z\|_2^2\le r\}\ge m$. A feasible measure minimizes precisely when it fills every fiber with $\|z\|_2^2<r$ to capacity and gives zero mass to every fiber with $\|z\|_2^2>r$. In particular there is a minimizer $
u_*$ with the same constant density relative to $\mu$ on all cutoff-shell fibers. It satisfies $
u_*(H)\le\mu(H)$ for every closed ambient halfspace $H$, and $
u_*(H)\ge m/2$ for every such $H$ containing zero.

pk-intake-three-homothetic-fibers-centro.relation_to_goal: A restricted sharp depth and point selection theorem for one integer coordinate and three positive homothetic fibers, with arbitrary translations and radii.
pk-intake-three-homothetic-fibers-centro.statement: Let $d\ge 2$ and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a full-dimensional compact convex body of volume $V$ and centroid zero. The only positive-volume integer fibers of a convex body in $\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ are $A=a+rK$, $B=b+RK$, and $C=c+sK$ at bases $-1,0,1$, respectively, with $r,R,s>0$ and $(A+C)/2\subseteq B$. Write $\gamma_d=(d/(d+1))^d$ and $M=V(r^d+R^d+s^d)$. Raw mass means the sum of the $d$-dimensional volumes of the traces on the actual integer fibers. If any fiber has volume at least $M/2$, the ordinary centroid of any such fiber has raw ambient halfspace depth at least $\gamma_d M/2$.
